job.title: Business Development Manager
job.description:
Stroke Aotearoa is looking for a commercially minded Business Development Account Manager to diversify revenue and build sustainable new income streams.

The opportunity

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll identify, develop and convert opportunities across partnerships, products and services. This is a genuine growth role, with revenue generation and commercial development at its core.

A key initial focus will be Health15, leading its commercial growth across market positioning, customer segmentation, pricing and sales. You’ll build the pipeline from prospecting through to negotiation, conversion and account growth across employers, health providers, insurers, government agencies and other partners.

You’ll also work closely with the CEO to identify new opportunities, assess their commercial potential and develop the partnerships and business cases to bring them to life.

About you

You’ll bring significant experience across business development, sales, commercial partnerships or growth, with evidence that you can create opportunities rather than simply manage established accounts.

You’ll be confident engaging with senior stakeholders, building external relationships and progressing opportunities through to commercial outcomes. Strong financial literacy and commercial judgement are important – you’ll need to understand pricing, investment, revenue potential, risk and ROI rather than treating BD purely as relationship management.

You’ll suit Stroke Aotearoa if you’re motivated by targets and growth but also want your commercial skills to contribute to something meaningful. Experience in health, disability, social impact or the not-for-profit sector would be advantageous rather than essential.

For the right person, this is a chance to build something: developing new markets, establishing long-term partnerships and creating revenue that directly supports Stroke Aotearoa’s mission to prevent stroke and improve lives.

job.title: Marketing Manager
job.description:
Stroke Aotearoa is the national charity dedicated solely to preventing stroke and improving the lives of stroke survivors, their whānau and carers. With an ambitious growth agenda, they are looking for an experienced Marketing Manager to lead their Marketing & Communications team and put marketing at the heart of how the organisation grows its reach, services and impact.

The opportunity

Reporting to the GM Marketing & Fundraising, this is a broad marketing leadership role with ownership across the full marketing mix – including strategy, brand, digital, campaigns, channels, audience engagement, market positioning and product and service development. You’ll lead a Communications Advisor and Marketing Officer, alongside managing external creative support.

A major focus will be bringing a stronger commercial, customer and product marketing lens to the organisation. You’ll use audience insight, market intelligence and performance data to identify opportunities, develop propositions and manage marketing across the full product and service lifecycle - from concept, positioning and go-to-market through to ongoing growth, optimisation and performance.

You’ll work across both established and emerging products and services, ensuring Stroke Aotearoa has a clear understanding of its audiences, strong market positioning and an integrated approach across paid, owned and earned channels. You’ll also partner closely with fundraising to ensure marketing activity contributes directly to supporter engagement and sustainable income growth.

About you

You’ll be an experienced marketing leader who can think strategically while remaining comfortable getting into delivery. You’ll bring broad experience across the marketing mix, with a strong understanding of brand, digital, campaigns, customer segmentation, product marketing and go-to-market strategy.

You’ll have experience taking products, services or initiatives from insight and concept through to launch and ongoing optimisation, with the ability to use data, customer insight and ROI to guide decisions.

Commercially minded and audience-focused, you’ll be capable of leading a small team while influencing across a wider organisation. Experience within health, disability, social impact or the not-for-profit sector would be useful, but isn’t essential.

This is an opportunity to take a well-known and highly respected purpose-led brand and shape how it markets itself, develops its offering and engages New Zealanders - ultimately helping Stroke Aotearoa grow its reach, revenue and impact.

job.title: People & Culture Business Partner (part-time)

Reporting to the CFO and working closely with the Chief Executive and senior leadership team, this is a varied role offering a great balance of business partnering, operational HR and continuous improvement.

Much of the groundwork has already been completed, including the development of core HR policies, performance management and remuneration frameworks. The opportunity now is to bring these to life, refine them as the organisation matures and provide practical, trusted people advice across the business.

About the Role:
With plenty of variety, responsibilities will include:
  •  Providing pragmatic, commercially sound HR and employment relations advice to leaders and managers. 
  •  Leading end-to-end recruitment activity, including supporting the establishment of a new investment team. 
  •  Embedding and further developing performance management processes, coaching managers and supporting review cycles. 
  •  Supporting the implementation of remuneration frameworks and annual review processes.

  •  Strengthening health, safety and wellbeing practices, working collaboratively with others across a shared workplace. 
  •  Maintaining accurate people records and ensuring effective day-to-day HR administration.
About You:
You'll be an experienced HR generalist and Business Partner who enjoys the breadth of the HR function and is equally comfortable advising senior leaders as you are rolling up your sleeves and getting things done.

You'll bring sound New Zealand employment legislation knowledge, recruitment capability and experience supporting performance management, remuneration and broader people initiatives.

Importantly, you'll be someone who:
  •  Is proactive, self-managing and confident working with a high degree of autonomy.
  •  Builds trusted relationships and communicates comfortably at all organisational levels.
  •  Enjoys coaching managers and building their confidence in people leadership.
  •  Brings a practical, solutions-focused approach and good professional judgement.
  •  Is adaptable, organised and comfortable working in an evolving environment.
  •  Genuinely enjoys the operational aspects of HR as well as contributing at a more strategic level.
  • You'll hold a relevant tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Business, Law or a related field, or bring equivalent relevant experience.
  • Experience within research, science or innovation environments, the technology sector or the public sector would be advantageous, as would exposure to establishing or improving HR frameworks.
Intrigued?
This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced P&C Business Partner looking for meaningful, varied work in a growing business with a positive, collaborative environment, supportive leadership and the opportunity to make a tangible contribution as its people practices continue to develop.

The role offers three days per week on a 12 month fixed term contract, with the potential for a longer-term arrangement; and it comes with an attractive remuneration package.

Apply NOW or contact Sharon Ward Duncan, Senior Consultant – 021 356 777 for a confidential chat and more information.

job.title: Health & Safety Business Partner
job.description:

Excellence in health, safety and wellbeing is critically important to providing high-quality care, and equally so for their external partners and all staff.

Role Overview:
As the Health & Safety Business Partner, you’ll provide leadership and operational expertise across the breadth of HS&W, working closely with senior leaders and operational managers to build a robust culture of safety, and take it to the next level from Good to Great.

Reporting to the Head of Quality, Risk and Assurance you will relish having a leader who will put high trust in you and support you when you need it. This pivotal role combines strategy and all the day-to-day functions of operational delivery, ensuring excellence in health and safety practices, systems, and risk management to safeguard their people and everyone they work with.

You'll enjoy working closely with the Clinical Advisor, Practice Advisor, and Quality Advisor who make up the team in Quality, Risk and Assurance; and the Learning & Development team will become close colleagues too.

As the subject matter expert in HSW, you'll quickly build good relationships throughout the organisation and become a trusted advisor who can influence change and hold leaders accountable for health & safety performance, through coaching and mentoring and escalation if needs be.

Key Responsibilities:
- Provide enterprise-wide strategic leadership and influence to embed a proactive, risk-based HSW framework that directly supports organisational performance, sustainability and risk maturity.

- Act as the organisation’s subject matter expert and trusted advisor to senior leaders and governance forums, shaping decision-making and organisational priorities through insight, analysis and evidence-based recommendations.

- Lead and embed an organisation-wide approach to HSW that is grounded in the organisation’s values, promotes care, responsibility and strong relationships, and supports a positive safety culture.

- Support the safety and wellbeing of employees and the people the organisation supports through strong systems, clear leadership accountability and continuous learning.

- Support the organisation to move from compliance-focused activity to a proactive, prevention-oriented and insight-led approach to health & safety.

- Working as part of the Quality, Risk and Assurance function, strengthen organisational capability, support leaders to take ownership of safety, and ensure the organisation meets its legislative, contractual and regulatory obligations.

About You:
- Demonstrated expertise in HS&W, ideally within the Healthcare sector, or within similar service sectors with a complex and multi-site environment.
- Strong knowledge of New Zealand’s HS&W legislation, proven risk management capability, and experience with audits and investigations.
- Proven ability to engage and influence at all organisational levels, from senior management to frontline.
- Adept with championing a whole-of-organisation approach to Health & Safety.
- A collaborative, values-based H&S business partner with a passion for creating culturally safe practice, and an inclusive and supportive environment for all.
- Flexible to travel regularly around the Auckland sites and to the other locations in Northland, Waikato, and Christchurch with some regularity.

For You:
- The opportunity is all about culture and influence to drive an impactful HS&W framework and initiatives that make a tangible difference to the lives of those in our community who are less able; and this will excite you!
- A collaborative and inclusive culture that values your expertise and empowers you to create positive change!
- An attractive remuneration package and 5 weeks' annual leave!

Ready to make an impact?
Join a great team and lift HSW from good to great!
